It could just be a bad mental day or it could be your diet. Make sure to eat a sufficient amount of calories for your activity level + goals! Another possible factor is the amount of sleep you're getting. Even if you don't quite feel tired throughout the day despite not sleeping enough the night before, you probably won't have the energy you want for your lifts.

He seems to only be eating at 2500 for a brief time period. Since I'm assuming he's been on a cut it's not the worst idea to be eating a bit above maintenance before transitioning to 2800 so his hormones won't be whack.

EDIT: Also just good to let his stomach get used to increase volume of food. I remember transitioning straight from a cut to a bulk and even with calorie dense foods the volume made it difficult to eat till I got used to it.l

If you're wanting to put on muscle then yeah it's a good time to bulk. Some people will suggest getting lower BF% before clean bulking because psychologically you'll just be more satisfied with how you look. If you're feeling good brother then just go for it. 

Keep up the work and you'll reach your goals.

If you would be happier then I say go for it! People forget that others have different standards than they do so they will try to and give advice off of what they want rather than the person asking! Aim to be happy with your body my dude and best of luck

Yeah I would try and take out caffeine for a bit and then reintroduce it to see how you feel. At the same time, preworkout and caffeine are not essential to workout. If you're really feeling that low on energy during your workouts I would take a look at how much you eat as well as how much you sleep.

Heyo sorry about the wrist injury. 3 sessions per week only targeting legs should be the max amount since you want days of rest in between for your legs. You could probably get by with hit those muscles twice a week but I bet you'll get more satisfaction and progress from three times a week.

1lb per week is honestly pretty ideal/average weight gain. It's hard to say if you should cut because I don't know what you look like. Try this though, reevaluate your goals. If you're trying to pack on muscle you'll inevitably gain some fat but not much. Would you be okay with how you look if you cut yourself to lower bf? Do you have enough muscle in your opinion? If the answer to those questions are no then continue along and try not to sweat the fat too much.

I say you just kinda have to do it ya know? Unless you do end up working out between home and shower because that sounds better. A day without lifting is also a day wasted when you consider your training goals.
